catalog_quote: p.35: "The regular accent in Wirangu is on the first syllable of a word, as is the case in all the surrounding languages. It is a fairly heavy stress accent (here marked by ' preceding the stressed syllable). The accent is accompanied by a high pitch intonation. There is a secondary stress on the third syllable of words of more than three syllables ..." p.36: "There is no doubt that phonemic length exists for the vowel a in the accented syllable in the neighbouring Thura-Yura languages Kuyani and Adnyamathanha, with minimal pairs such as marni 'fat' and maarni 'husband'." p.1: "... the Wirangu, had affiliations with their neighbours to the east and north-east, with the Kuyani and the Nauo groups ... All these people spoke languages belonging to the Thura-Yura group." Preface p.xv: "... while working on the two neighbouring languages, Kuyani and Mirniny."
world_status: statement found in an open source
sweep_summary: Guyani (Kuyani, gvy) is not in the catalog and this search of works with stress in the title produced exactly one title hit, Meguerditchian, Vuillemin & Pruetz 2017 'Identifying the ape beat in the wild..' (EVOLANG 12, doi:10.12775/3991-1.072). downloaded the open PDF (2 pp.) and read it: it is about chimpanzees slapping baobab fruit in Senegal and says nothing about any human language; Glottolog's own record shows language code 'Guyani [gvy] (computerized assignment from "fruit")', i.e. a keyword mis-tag. Relevance not relevant, priority none; it should be dropped from the gvy bibliography. Beyond the item list I looked for any first-hand Kuyani stress statement: Simpson & Hercus 2004 'Thura-Yura as a subgroup' is closed at Benjamins (OpenAlex: no OA) and embargoed on the ANU repository (hdl 1885/81147, 401) — medium priority to acquire; Hercus's unpublished Kuyani vocabulary/sketch grammar and her AIATSIS tapes (listed on the Mobile Language Team source archive) are the only descriptive materials and are not online — high priority; Hercus & White 1973 (open, ANU) and the MLT Kuyani sounds lesson were read and are silent on stress. For context only, Schebeck 1974 (Adnyamathanha, PL D-21, open at hdl 1885/145158) p. xvii states first-syllable primary stress with secondary stress tending to the penult — a sister variety, not Guyani. the best new statement: none for Guyani. Everything downloaded is under with.org APIs, the ANU DSpace API and direct downloads

All three quoted passages are present verbatim at the stated locators: (1) sec. 2.2.2(a) 'Accent and pitch', book p.35 (PDF p.57): "The regular accent in Wirangu is on the first syllable of a word, as is the case in all the surrounding languages. new_statements.rule_in_words: Word accent falls on the first syllable; Hercus (the principal Kuyani fieldworker) states this for Wirangu and extends it to 'all the surrounding languages', among which she explicitly counts the Thura-Yura language Kuyani on the same and adjacent pages (where the 'accented syllable' of Kuyani marni/maarni is the first). This is an areal first-hand remark, not a dedicated Kuyani description. The closest relative Adnyamathanha (adny1235; Hercus 1979 treats Guyani and Adnyamathanha as dialects of one language, >80% cognate) is independently described with first-syllable primary stress (Schebeck 1974: xvii; Schebeck 1973: 29).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing stated for Kuyani. (Wirangu: secondary stress on the third syllable of words of more than three syllables; Adnyamathanha per Schebeck 1974: secondary stress tends to fall on the penult.)
new_statements.exceptions: None for Kuyani. (Wirangu: accent may shift to the final syllable in emphatic vocatives/imperatives and optionally onto long aa created by g-elision in -gardu forms.) Hercus 1999:36 notes Kuyani also has long vowels in second syllables from elision of k in the suffix -(k)aka, e.g. kadnya(k)aka, without comment on accent.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level accent ('first syllable of a word'); statement is about Wirangu with an explicit areal generalisation covering neighbouring languages including Kuyani.
new_statements.identity_note: No dedicated published description of Kuyani/Guyani (guya1249) exists; the quoted statement is Hercus's areal remark in her Wirangu (wira1265) grammar, which names Kuyani as a neighbouring Thura-Yura language on the same pages. The closest relative, Adnyamathanha (adny1235), which Hercus 1979 treats as a co-dialect of Guyani (>80% cognate, mutually intelligible), has explicit first-syllable-stress statements in Schebeck 1974: xvii and Schebeck 1973: 29 (files and guya1249). Dixon 2002 and Wikipedia merge Kuyani into Adnyamathanha.

sources.note: sec. 2.2.2(a) p.35: regular accent in Wirangu on the first syllable 'as is the case in all the surrounding languages'; secondary stress on 3rd syllable. p.36 refers to phonemic vowel length 'in the accented syllable in the neighbouring Thura-Yura languages Kuyani and Adnyamathanha' (marni/maarni).
